root_cause.text: The reset-gpio driver creates a dynamic device that is intended to persist indefinitely, but lacks a proper devlink to its consumer, so allowing user-space to unbind the device via sysfs leads to a use-after-free when the reset control handle is released.
root_cause.evidence: The patch suppresses sysfs bind attributes by setting `suppress_bind_attrs = true` in the `reset_gpio_driver` structure, explicitly stating that unbinding would cause a use-after-free splat from any user that puts the reset control handle.

intent_record.intent_summary: Suppress bind attributes for reset-gpio auxiliary driver to prevent manual unbinding.
intent_record.what: Added `.suppress_bind_attrs = true` to the `driver` field of the `reset_gpio_driver` auxiliary driver structure.
intent_record.how: Prevents the creation of sysfs bind/unbind attributes for the reset-gpio driver, disabling manual unbinding or rebinding via userspace.

grouping_result.intent: Suppress bind attributes for reset-gpio auxiliary driver to prevent manual unbinding.

relevance_review.reason: The group suppresses bind attributes for the reset-gpio auxiliary driver, directly preventing user-space from manually unbinding the device via sysfs, which is the exact trigger for the use-after-free described in the vulnerability root cause.

candidates.rationale: This line begins the driver structure definition that, by default, does not include suppress_bind_attrs, allowing user-space to unbind the device via sysfs and trigger use-after-free.

This macro registers the driver on the auxiliary bus, which creates bind/unbind sysfs attributes by default, enabling the unbind operation that leads to use-after-free when the reset control handle is released.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit cee544a40e4426040946e685988b1489f13e6600
Author: Krzysztof Kozlowski <krzk@kernel.org>
Date:   Mon Jan 29 12:52:13 2024 +0100

    reset: gpio: Add GPIO-based reset controller
    
    Add a simple driver to control GPIO-based resets using the reset
    controller API for the cases when the GPIOs are shared and reset should
    be coordinated.  The driver is expected to be used by reset core
    framework for ad-hoc reset controllers.
    
    Cc: Bartosz Golaszewski <brgl@bgdev.pl>
    C
bic_trace_step.reason: The entire driver code is shown. It registers a reset controller via devm_reset_controller_register() but does not create a device link (devlink) to its consumer. Without a devlink, user-space unbinding via sysfs would free the device while consumers may still hold reset control handles, leading to use-after-free. No protection against unbinding is present.

    reset: gpio: convert the driver to using the auxiliary bus
    
    As the reset-gpio devices are purely virtual and never instantiated from
    real firmware nodes, let's convert the driver to using the - more
    fitting - auxiliary bus.
    
    Reviewed-by: Philipp Zabel <p.zabel@pengutronix.de>
    Acked-by: Linus Walleij <linus.walleij@linaro.org>
    Ac
bic_trace_step.reason: The probe function does not create a device link (e.g., device_link_add) between the reset device and its consumer. The absence of this devlink is the root cause of the use-after-free vulnerability when user-space unbinds the device via sysfs. The commit only changes the bus type from platform to auxiliary without adding the necessary link, so the vulnerable construct remains and the fix is not present.
